title: Taking retirement-plan money: the 25% test that makes an entity's assets ERISA plan assets
rule: An entity's assets are plan assets if benefit plan investors hold 25 percent or more of any class of its equity by value after any equity acquisition, unless an exception, such as for qualifying operating companies, applies. Benefit plan investors are ERISA part 4 plans, Code section 4975 plans (individual retirement accounts included) and plan-asset entities. Equity of anyone with control or paid advice over the assets, or an affiliate, is disregarded unless held by a benefit plan investor, such as a principal's retirement account. From 25 percent, such persons become each investing plan's fiduciaries and may not self-deal. Counsel checks a principal's retirement-account investment for a possible prohibited transaction.
changeWatch: Amendments to 29 U.S.C. 1002(42) or 29 CFR 2510.3-101, Labor Department guidance on the operating-company exceptions, or changes to the plans covered by Code section 4975. The card follows the statute's benefit plan investor definition; 29 CFR 2510.3-101(f)(2)(i) still reads more broadly.
